Weight-license must be verified at download (community HF mirrors label MIT, but the base models were trained on large corpora); low risk for a personal local project, non-zero for redistribution.
Two toolchains (GPT-SoVITS + RVC) with separate Python/PyTorch env pins on macOS add real setup/maintenance fragility vs a single-model solution.

debates.argument:
Chatterbox is the strongest honest pick for a local, free, fine-tunable ChinAI voice. LICENSE: base repo resemble-ai/chatterbox is MIT (redistributable, commercial-OK); fine-tune toolkits are MIT (stlohrey, davidbrowne17) and Apache-2.0 (gokhaneraslan). No gated weights, no non-commercial clause. Perth watermark is embedded in outputs (imperceptible; does not affect blind-test indistinguishability).

WHY IT CAN GET INDISTINGUISHABLE: it already does strong zero-shot cloning from a 6s reference; fine-tuning on 30-60 min locks the owner's timbre, cadence and idiolect rather than approximating it. The 0.5B Llama T3 stage is what you train; the S3Gen flow-matching vocoder + voice encoder stay frozen, so you are adapting a standard HF Llama transformer — the best-understood thing to fine-tune. Two real prosody dials (exaggeration, cfg_weight) give genuine expressive control at inference, so you tune identity once and steer delivery per-utterance.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION (train+infer on Apple Silicon, no CUDA): verified in source, not README claims. Base pyproject and ALL THREE finetune toolkits contain ZERO CUDA-only dependencies — no bitsandbytes, DeepSpeed, flash-attn, or xformers; just torch 2.6 + transformers (+ peft for LoRA). stlohrey/finetune_t3.py drives full T3 fine-tune through HuggingFace Trainer, which auto-detects and runs on MPS; it loads on cpu and lets Trainer place the model. gokhaneraslan uses peft==0.17.1 LoRA (Apache-2.0, updated 2026-06), explicitly recommending LoRA for <10h datasets — the 30-60 min case — and LoRA on a Llama backbone runs on MPS in ~16GB unified RAM. davidbrowne17 guards every CUDA-specific op (autocast/GradScaler/pin_memory) behind if DEVICE=='cuda' and ships example_for_mac.py. MPS inference is well-proven (multiple Apple-Silicon ports, 2-3x over CPU).
debates.local_mac_finetune_realistic: yes, with a documented caveat — it is feasible, not turnkey. Feasible because the hard blockers are absent: no toolkit depends on bitsandbytes/DeepSpeed/flash-attn/xformers, the trainable part is a standard HF Llama transformer, and both training paths (HF Trainer, peft LoRA) support MPS; MPS inference is already proven. Recommended route: gokhaneraslan peft-LoRA path on an M-series Mac (>=16GB), fp32 or partial-bf16 (NOT fp16 — MPS autocast/GradScaler are CUDA-only), PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 for the odd unsupported op. Caveats that keep this from a clean 'turnkey yes': (1) no repo advertises a *tested* MPS training run — example_for_mac.py is inference-only, so expect a one-line device patch (add 'mps' to the cuda/cpu ternary; skip the hardcoded whisper device=cuda auto-transcribe by pre-transcribing); (2) fp32 training of even a LoRA over a 0.5B backbone on MPS is slow — plan hours per run and memory pressure, full fine-tune wants ~24GB; (3) 'indistinguishable in a blind test' is the honest ceiling, not a guarantee — 30-60 min plus LoRA reliably reaches high speaker-similarity/naturalness, but occasional artifacts and prosody misses are likely without iteration on data quality (clean 24k mono, VAD-trimmed).
debates.strongest_point: Verified in source that neither the base package nor any of the three fine-tuning toolkits pull a single CUDA-only dependency (no bitsandbytes/DeepSpeed/flash-attn/xformers) — the trainable component is a plain HuggingFace Llama transformer trained via HF Trainer or peft-LoRA, both of which run on MPS, so the usual reason 'it won't train on a Mac' simply does not apply here.
key_risks: No fine-tune repo ships a *tested* MPS training path; example_for_mac.py is inference-only, so a small device patch (add 'mps', disable fp16/GradScaler, pre-transcribe to avoid hardcoded whisper device=cuda) is required before training starts.
fp16 autocast + GradScaler are CUDA-only; on MPS you must train fp32 or partial-bf16 (torch 2.6 MPS bf16 is incomplete), which is slower and heavier on unified memory.

MPS training speed/memory: hours per run for LoRA on a 0.5B backbone; full fine-tune realistically wants ~24GB unified RAM, and some ops may CPU-fallback (PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK) further slowing it.
'Indistinguishable in a blind test' is the aspiration, not a floor — outcome depends heavily on clean, VAD-trimmed 24k data and iteration; expect occasional artifacts/prosody misses.
All outputs carry Resemble's Perth watermark (imperceptible to humans, so not a blind-test problem, but present and worth disclosing).
Every fine-tune toolkit is a third-party community repo (105-291 stars), not Resemble-maintained — durability and future compatibility are on you to pin (torch 2.6 / transformers 4.46.3).
